title: Unpacking the Determinants of Financial Resilience in the Philippines
venue: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Discussion Paper Series
tldr: Demographics尤其是income quintile and gender are stronger predictors of Filipino financial resilience than financial inclusion indicators, as shown by Logistic LASSO, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models on Global Findex 2017 and 2021 data.
problem_and_motivation: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed deep financial vulnerabilities among Filipino households, yet the determinants of individual-level financial resilience in the Philippines remain understudied. Financial inclusion does not guarantee financial resilience.
approach: Used World Bank Global Findex surveys for the Philippines (2017: 980 respondents; 2021: 992 respondents).
Constructed 23 binary, ordinal, and numeric predictors based on Salignac et al. (2019) Multidimensional Financial Resilience Framework.
Applied Logistic Regression, Logistic LASSO, Decision Tree, Random Forest, LDA, Naive Bayes, KNN, SVM, and Neural Network classifiers.
Evaluated models using accuracy scores, ROC curves, and confusion matrices.
Generated inferences on feature importance from Logistic LASSO coefficients, Decision Tree splits, and Random Forest feature importance rankings.
findings: num: Test accuracy across all models ranged from 59-65% (2017) and 62-68% (2021), all below 70 percent.
Income quintile was the top predictor of financial resilience in both 2017 and 2021.
Gender (female) was consistently negatively associated with financial resilience, with the gap widening from 2017 to 2021.
num: Mobile phone ownership rose from 75.8% in 2017 to 96.3% in 2021; financial account ownership rose from 34.3% to 56.8%.
Saving for retirement was the second-strongest positive predictor of financial resilience after income quintile.
Tertiary education jumped from minimal coefficient in 2017 to second only to income quintile in 2021.
Medical borrowing emerged as a strong negative predictor in 2021 but was uninformative in 2017.
Demographics provide higher predictive value for financial resilience than financial access indicators.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: One of the first Philippine-context empirical analyses of determinants of individual-level financial resilience using machine learning classifiers. Demonstrates that demographic factors outperform financial inclusion indicators in predicting resilience.
directly_justifies: Income quintile, saving behavior, and gender are the top predictors of Filipino financial resilience.
Demographics provide higher predictive value for financial resilience than financial access indicators.
The gender gap in financial resilience widened from 2017 to 2021 despite higher female financial account ownership.
Medical borrowing became a strong negative predictor of financial resilience in 2021.
Online payment predictive power decreased from 2017 to 2021 as adoption became widespread.
limits: Test accuracy remained below 70% across all models.
2021 phone-based survey mode excluded respondents without phone access.
Predominantly binary nature of Findex variables limits feature interactions.

limitations: All models achieved test accuracy below 70%, indicating substantial unmeasured factors.
The Global Findex proxy for financial resilience is narrow and does not capture multidimensional nature.
Cross-sectional survey data prevents causal interpretation.
The 2021 shift to phone-based surveys introduced selection bias.
Predominantly binary variables limit model complexity.
Lack of variables such as geographic location, occupation, and home ownership may reduce model accuracy.
remember_this: Income quintile, saving behavior, and gender are the top predictors of Filipino financial resilience across all models.
Demographics consistently outperform financial inclusion indicators in predicting financial resilience.
All ML models achieved below 70% accuracy, signaling important unmeasured determinants.
The gender gap in financial resilience widened from 2017 to 2021 despite increased female financial inclusion.
Medical borrowing emerged as a significant negative predictor only in 2021.
